info.title: Joinways Public API
info.description:
The Joinways REST API lets you read and manage your CRM and event data:
events, quotes, companies, contacts, leads (requests), venues, catalog,
tasks, reports and more. It is a **JSON over HTTPS** API described by
this OpenAPI 3.1 document, served at `https://joinways.app/openapi.yaml`
and rendered at `https://joinways.app/docs/api`.

The same data is reachable from AI assistants through the Joinways MCP
server (`https://mcp.joinways.app`, guide at
`https://joinways.app/docs/claude-mcp`): both surfaces share the OAuth
server, the tokens, the scopes, the role permissions and the services of
the app, so a rule holds the same way in the app, in the REST API and in
MCP.

## Authentication

Every request needs a **Bearer token** in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer jw_xxxxxxxx
```

Two token types work:

- **API key** (`jw_…`): an owner or admin creates one from **Settings →
  Developers → API keys** in the workspace (guide:
  `https://joinways.app/docs/api-keys`). An API key acts as the member
  who created it: it carries the read and write scopes, and the **role
  permissions its creator holds now** in the workspace (see below; a
  creator who leaves the workspace takes the key's access with them). It
  does not expire unless you set an expiry, and can be revoked at any
  time from the same page.
- **OAuth 2.1 access token** (`jw_oat_…`): for apps acting on a user's
  behalf (Authorization Code + PKCE S256, same flow as the MCP server).
  - Authorization endpoint `https://joinways.app/oauth/authorize`, token
    endpoint `https://joinways.app/api/oauth/token`, revocation
    `https://joinways.app/api/oauth/revoke` (RFC 7009), metadata
    `https://joinways.app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.
  - **Clients**: register with Dynamic Client Registration
    (`POST /api/oauth/register`), or use an https URL as `client_id`
    (Client ID Metadata Document).
  - **Resource** (RFC 8707): send `resource=https://joinways.app/api/v1`
    on the authorization and token requests to bind the token to this API
    (a token bound to `https://mcp.joinways.app` is refused here, and the
    other way round). An unknown resource is refused with
    `invalid_target`. Protected resource metadata:
    `https://joinways.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/v1`.
  - **Refresh**: a client registered with the `refresh_token` grant gets a
    refresh token (`jw_ort_…`) next to a **1 hour** access token. Each
    refresh rotates the refresh token (the old one stops working); a
    refresh token unused for 90 days expires. A client without the
    refresh grant gets a **30 day** access token and re-runs the flow.
    A refresh may ask for fewer scopes: only the new access token is
    narrowed. A user who left the workspace gets `invalid_grant` on
    refresh, and the whole token family is revoked.
  - **Granted scope** = requested ∩ supported (`mcp.read`, `mcp.write`)
    ∩ registered by the client.
  - The authorization response carries `iss` (RFC 9207). The consent
    screen shows the host of a metadata-document client, and warns when
    the `redirect_uri` is on another domain.
  - A workspace owner sees and revokes connected apps in **Settings →
    Developers → MCP → Connected apps**.

A token is **bound to a single workspace**. You never pass an
`account_id`: the workspace comes from the token. The API is part of
the **Pro plan and the free trial**: a valid token of a workspace
without either is refused with `403 forbidden`, `details.reason:
plan_not_eligible`. Revocation takes effect within about a minute
across our infrastructure. Tokens are stored hashed (SHA-256) and shown
once.

A `401` carries the RFC 6750 / RFC 9728 challenge:

```
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://joinways.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/v1", scope="mcp.read mcp.write"
```

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `mcp.read` | Every `GET` |
| `mcp.write` | Every `POST`, `PATCH`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, and reading (it implies `mcp.read`) |

API keys carry both scopes. A scope never grants more than the role of
the token owner allows.

## Roles and permissions

The API applies the same role rules as the app. Each operation names the
permission it needs in its description and in the
`x-required-permission` extension (a list means **any** of them); without
it, a `403 forbidden` is returned with `Missing required permission: …`.
Operations without `x-required-permission` are open to every member.

| Permission | owner | admin | member | operations | viewer | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data.write` | yes | yes | yes | yes | | Event details, archiving and unarchiving events, BEO, notes, tasks, staff, contacts, slots, people, companies, sending emails, deleting one's own webhook |
| `events.manage` | yes | yes | yes | | | Creating events, changing an event status or stage |
| `leads.manage` | yes | yes | yes | | | **Reading** and processing requests (`/leads*`) |
| `quotes.manage` | yes | yes | yes | | | Quotes, quote items, catalog items, signed quote import |
| `reports.view` | yes | yes | yes | | yes | Analytics |
| `reports.view` or `quotes.manage` | yes | yes | yes | | yes | **Reading** quotes and event amounts; **writing** event amounts |
| `settings.manage` | yes | yes | | | | Venue opening hours, closures, holidays; deleting events and people |
| `integrations.manage` | yes | yes | | | | Webhooks |

Reads follow the role too: without `leads.manage` the `/leads*` reads
answer `403`; without `reports.view` or `quotes.manage` the quote reads
answer `403` and the amounts of an event (`budget`, `expected_revenue`,
`confirmed_amount`, `confirmed_amount_excl_tax`,
`cancellation_fee_excl_tax`) are `null`, and writing one of them
answers `403` with `details.reason: revenue_access_required`. Venues
and their catalog are
limited to the venues the member can see (a member limited to some
venues gets `404` on the others; `settings.manage` sees them all).

## Pagination

List endpoints take `page` (1-based, default `1`) and `per_page`
(default `50`, max `500`) and return:

```json
{
  "data": [],
  "pagination": { "page": 1, "per_page": 50, "total": 1234, "total_pages": 25 }
}
```

A page past the last one returns `200` with `data: []` (its `total` may
then be `null`). Lists that are not paginated say so.

## Errors

Errors use standard HTTP status codes and one body:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "conflict", "message": "Event is archived: unarchive it before editing it", "details": { "reason": "event_archived" } } }
```

| Status | `code` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | Validation failed (`details` holds the field errors), an id of the body is not in the workspace, or an id filter of the query is not a UUID (`details.field` names it) |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token, or a token bound to another resource |
| 402 | `payment_required` | The workspace plan does not include the feature (quotes) |
| 403 | `forbidden` | Missing scope or role permission, workspace without Pro plan or trial (`plan_not_eligible`), amounts written without revenue access (`revenue_access_required`), or a lead locked by the Free plan (`lead_locked`) |
| 404 | `not_found` | Not in this workspace (or outside the member's venues), or the id of the path is not a UUID |
| 409 | `conflict` | The state of the record refuses the operation; `details.reason` is a stable code (e.g. `event_archived`, `event_not_archived`, `venue_unavailable`, `quote_locked`) |
| 409 | `idempotency_conflict` | The request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still running |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` | Upload over the limit (signed quote PDF: 4 MB) |
| 422 | `idempotency_key_reuse` | `Idempotency-Key` reused with another method, path or body |
| 422 | `quota_exceeded` | Workspace quota reached (25 active webhooks) |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Too many requests: wait for `Retry-After` seconds |
| 500 | `server_error` | Unexpected error (no internal detail, never a database message) |

A refusal of the record's state is always a `409`, never a `500`. Branch
on `code` and `details.reason`, not on `message` (English, may change).
`details.reason` is always snake_case lower case, the same value as the
`code` of the matching MCP tool error; the reasons of each domain are
listed in the `ErrorReason` schema (components). Validation errors of the
query carry `details.field`.

## Rate limits

Two limits stack on every request:

| Layer | Limit |
|---|---|
| Per IP, before authentication | 300 requests / minute |
| Per workspace, **Pro** plan | 600 requests / minute and 100,000 / day |
| Per workspace, **free trial** | 200 requests / minute and 5,000 / day |
| Sending emails (`POST /events/{id}/emails`, shared with MCP) | 20 / minute per workspace |

Every response carries the current budget (the per-minute workspace
budget once authenticated, the IP budget before):

```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 587
X-RateLimit-Reset: 2026-10-04T14:31:00.000Z
```

Every `429` carries `Retry-After` (seconds), the `X-RateLimit-*` of the
budget it exhausted, and `details.reason`: `per-ip`,
`per-account-minute`, `per-account-day` or `email_rate_limited`. Wait
for it, then back off exponentially.

## Idempotency

Every mutating request (`POST`, `PATCH`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) accepts an
optional `Idempotency-Key` header: a client-generated key of 1 to 255
characters (a UUID v4 works well). Retrying with the same key within
**24 hours** returns the response recorded for the first attempt, marked
`Idempotency-Replayed: true`, instead of executing the operation again.

- Keys are scoped to the workspace **and the user**: two members (or
  their integrations) choosing the same key never replay each other.
- The request identity is the method, the path, the **query string**
  and the body. Same key with a **different** request: `422`
  `idempotency_key_reuse`. A multipart upload is compared on its fields
  and the SHA-256 of its files (the multipart boundary may change).
- Retry while the first request is **still running**: `409`
  `idempotency_conflict`; wait briefly, then retry.
- Final `2xx` / `4xx` responses are recorded, except a `429` and a
  transient `409` (`details.reason` `lead_moved_concurrently`,
  `version_conflict`, `amendment_in_flight`): after those, and after a
  `5xx`, the key is released and a retry with the same key runs again.
- Keys expire after 24 hours and may then be reused.

## Webhooks

`POST /webhooks` subscribes an https endpoint to these events:

| Type | Sent when | Extra fields |
|---|---|---|
| `lead.created` | A request arrives | |
| `lead.archived` | A request is archived | |
| `lead.merged` | A duplicate request is merged into another | `merged_into_lead_id` |
| `event.created` | An event is created | |
| `event.status_changed` | The status changes | `previous_status`, `new_status` |
| `event.stage_changed` | The custom stage changes | `previous_stage_id`, `new_stage_id`, `new_stage_name` |
| `quote.created` | A quote is created | |
| `quote.status_changed` | A quote status changes | `previous_status`, `new_status` |

Each delivery is a JSON `POST`:
`{ "event_type", "account_id", "occurred_at", "data", … }`. `data` is the
record in the shape the API returns it: an item of `GET /events`, of
`GET /leads` (plus the request's descriptive fields; locked leads
sealed), or the `quote` object of `GET /quotes/{id}`. The record is read
again when the delivery is built, never taken from the trigger.

Headers:

- `X-Joinways-Event`: the event type.
- `X-Joinways-Delivery`: a UUID, the same across the retries of one
  delivery. Deduplicate on it.
- `X-Joinways-Timestamp`: Unix seconds.
- `X-Joinways-Signature-V2: sha256=<hex>`: HMAC-SHA256 of
  `<timestamp>.<raw body>` with the subscription `secret`. Check it, and
  reject a timestamp older than 5 minutes to refuse replays.
- `X-Joinways-Signature: sha256=<hex>`: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body
  (first version, kept for existing receivers).

Delivery: 3 quick attempts, then retries after 10 minutes, 30 minutes,
2 hours, 6 hours and 24 hours on a network error, a timeout, a `5xx`, a
`408` or a `429`. A `410 Gone` answer deletes the subscription; 10
failed deliveries in a row disable it (`disabled_at`). Targets must be
public https URLs; redirects are not followed.

## Security

- **Transport:** HTTPS only.
- **At rest:** API keys and OAuth tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes;
  the raw value is shown once.
- **OAuth 2.1:** Authorization Code flow with mandatory PKCE (S256),
  exact `redirect_uri` match, single-use codes valid 10 minutes, refresh
  token rotation.
- **Tenant isolation:** every token is scoped to one workspace; an id of
  another workspace answers `404` (path) or `400` (body).
- **Never returned:** internal search vectors and embeddings, and the
  capability tokens of public pages (`public_token`,
  `beo_public_token`; the BEO page link is given as `beo_public_url`).

## Conventions

- Timestamps are **ISO 8601** (`2026-10-04T14:30:00Z`); days are
  `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- IDs are UUIDs (notifications use an integer id).
- The product term **venue** maps to the internal `location` (events
  expose `venue_id`; a few responses also keep `location_id`).
- An **archived event is read-only**: every write on it or on its
  sub-resources answers `409` (`details.reason: event_archived`).
  Archive and unarchive with `POST /events/{id}/archive` and
  `POST /events/{id}/unarchive`.

## Changelog

### 1.4.0 (2026-10-04)

Breaking changes (security and role rules):

- **Reads follow the role**: `GET /leads*` needs `leads.manage`;
  `GET /quotes*` (and the quote PDF) needs `reports.view` or
  `quotes.manage`; event amounts are `null` without one of them.
- **Webhooks** need `integrations.manage` to be created; a webhook is
  deleted by its creator or by `integrations.manage`; the list masks
  `target_url` (origin only) without `integrations.manage`.
- **Sending an email** (`POST /events/{id}/emails`) needs `data.write`
  and is queued: `202` with `outbox_id` and `send_after` (cancellable
  for 30 seconds from the event's emails tab), signature of the mailbox
  added; no more `502` / `503`.
- **`DELETE /events/{id}`** only deletes an archived event (`409
  event_not_archived` otherwise) and needs `settings.manage`.
- **Removed fields**: `embedding`, `search_vector`, `public_token`,
  `beo_public_token` (use `beo_public_url`) and the unused quote
  `amount`.
- Venue opening hours, closures and holidays need `settings.manage`;
  venues and catalog are limited to the member's venues.
- A closure cannot be created with `closureType: holiday` (use
  `POST /venues/{venueId}/holidays`).
- A workspace without Pro plan or trial gets `403 forbidden`
  (`plan_not_eligible`) instead of `401`.
- `details.reason` is snake_case lower case everywhere (quote reasons
  were upper case: `QUOTE_LOCKED` is now `quote_locked`); quote error
  messages are in English.
- Writing event amounts without `reports.view` or `quotes.manage` is
  refused (`403 revenue_access_required`).
- `GET` / `PATCH /leads/{id}` return the list fields plus the request's
  descriptive fields (`subject`, `ai_summary`, `requirements`…), no
  longer the internal columns.
- An id of the path that is not a UUID answers `404`; an id filter of
  the query that is not a UUID answers `400` with `details.field`
  (both used to be `500`).
- `GET /events/{id}/notes`, `/tasks` and `/emails` answer `404` for an
  event of another workspace or unknown (was an empty list).
- Idempotency keys are scoped per user; the query string is part of the
  request identity; `429` and transient `409` are not replayed.

Additions and fixes:

- New `POST /events/{id}/archive`, `POST /events/{id}/unarchive`,
  `GET /tasks/{id}` and `POST /leads/{id}/merge`.
- `PATCH /events/{id}` with `status` has the effects of
  `POST /events/{id}/status`; dates are checked only when sent; an
  unknown or foreign venue is `400 invalid_reference`.
- Convert: `400 invalid_dates`, `409 venue_locked`, `details.reason` on
  every refusal; merge: `403 lead_locked`.
- `POST /leads` creates the sibling request of another venue (`201`).
- Quotes: `POST` / `PATCH` return the cleaned `document_lines` like
  `GET`; an explicit `currency` is kept.
- Expired notifications are left out. A `tiered` catalog item keeps its
  mode on a partial update.
- Unexpected database errors are a `500 server_error` without the
  database message.
- `POST /events`: `end_date` defaults to `start_date`, `venue_id` to the
  only active venue; new `timezone`, `contact_person_id`,
  `assigned_to_account_id`, `company_id`, `source`.
- `GET /events/{id}`: flat `company_name`, `venue_name`, `contact_*`,
  `billing_company_id`, `quote_to_platform` next to the nested objects.
- `PATCH /events/{id}`: `stage_id`, `timezone`, `quote_to_platform`,
  `billing_company_id`, `confirmed_amount_excl_tax`, `selected_dates`.
- `POST /events/{id}/status`: `stage_id`, loss and cancellation reasons,
  group siblings, notifications and calendars like the app.
- `GET /events?to=` includes the whole day; `type` takes several values.
- Archived events are read-only on every sub-resource (`409`).
- Leads: real schema and statuses (`pending`, `validated`, `rejected`,
  `needs_info`), `inquiry_key`; `POST /leads` takes `platform_link` /
  `platform` and returns the existing request instead of a duplicate
  (`existing`, `matched_via`); `POST /leads/{id}/link` uses the app's
  rules; convert returns the mapped event.
- Quotes: `GET /quotes/{id}` documented as `{ quote, items }`; state
  refusals are `409 conflict` with `details.reason`; `currency` is an
  ISO 4217 enum defaulting to the venue's; quote items accept
  `event_day_date` and `discount_percent` on update.
- Catalog: `pricing_mode`, `vat_rate` alias, `event_id` pricing,
  `type` filter. People: `job_title` alias of `role`. Companies: `state`.
- Search filters on `types`. Notifications are the token owner's own.
- Webhooks: `quote.created`, `event.stage_changed`, `lead.archived`,
  `lead.merged`; signature v2 with timestamp and delivery id; retries.
- OAuth: refresh tokens, `resource` (RFC 8707), Client ID Metadata
  Documents, `iss` in the authorization response, granted scope limited
  to the client's registration. Webhook secrets and target URLs are no
  longer readable by members through the database.
- `X-RateLimit-*` on every response, `Retry-After` on every `429`.
- Idempotency keys apply to every write, multipart uploads included.

get.description: Events of the workspace, newest start date first by default. Archived events are left out unless `archived` says otherwise. The sample events created at onboarding are never listed. Amounts are `null` without `reports.view` or `quotes.manage`. **Role permission:** none (any member).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to sort by. Any other value sorts by `start_date`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: One or more statuses (repeat the parameter or separate with commas).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: One or more event types (repeat the parameter or separate with commas).

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description: Only events of this company.

parameters.name: venue_id
parameters.description: Only events at this venue.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Lower bound on `start_date` (inclusive), `YYYY-MM-DD` or an ISO timestamp.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Upper bound on `start_date`, inclusive. A `YYYY-MM-DD` day covers that whole day (UTC); an ISO timestamp is used as is.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match on the event title.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: `exclude` (default) hides archived events, `only` shows only them, `all` shows both.

200.description: Page of events. A page past the last one is empty.

400.description: An id filter is not a UUID (`details.field` names it).

post.description: Creates an event with the app's rules: venue availability (`block` mode refuses a closure or hours outside opening, `409`), locked venue refused, rooms of the venue only, contact and company found or created, a booking platform name given as `company_name` becomes the event `source` instead of a client company, calendars synchronised. The response is the stored event; `warnings` lists what could not be done (`space_ids_not_booked`). **Role permission:** `events.manage`.

warnings.description: Only present when something could not be done.

400.description: Validation failed. `details.reason`: `venue_required` (several or no active venue: pass `venue_id`), `invalid_dates` (unreadable date, or end before start), `invalid_timezone`, `invalid_reference` (an id, venue included, of another workspace or unknown), `invalid_assignee` (not a member), `invalid_venue_spaces`.

403.description: Missing permission, or `budget` sent without `reports.view` or `quotes.manage` (`details.reason` `revenue_access_required`, `details.field`).

409.description: `details.reason`: `venue_unavailable` (closure or outside opening hours in `block` mode, with `violation`, `closures`, `outside_hours`) or `venue_locked` (venue locked by the Free plan).

get.description: The event with its booked rooms (`spaces`), its slots, the company, venue and contact both nested (`companies`, `locations`, `people`) and flat (`company_name`, `venue_name`, `contact_*`), and the public BEO link. Amounts are `null` without `reports.view` or `quotes.manage`. **Role permission:** none (any member).

patch.description: Updates the given fields with the app's rules: archived event refused, end after start (checked when dates are sent), locked venue refused, venue availability, time zone following a venue change, billed party pushed to the unsigned quotes, calendars synchronised, timeline entries. Omitted fields stay as they are. With `status`, the status change has the effects of `POST /events/{id}/status` (notification, reasons cleared, Slack, calendars, webhook); the other fields are written first, so a refused field never leaves a half-applied status. **Role permission:** `data.write`; changing `status` or `stage_id` also needs `events.manage`.

400.description: Validation failed. `details.reason`: `invalid_dates`, `invalid_timezone`, `invalid_reference` (venue or id of another workspace, or unknown), `invalid_assignee`, `invalid_stage`, `invalid_venue_spaces`, `no_fields`.

403.description: Missing permission (`events.manage` for `status` / `stage_id`), or an amount (`budget`, `confirmed_amount_excl_tax`) sent without `reports.view` or `quotes.manage` (`details.reason` `revenue_access_required`, `details.field`).

409.description: `details.reason`: `event_archived`, `venue_locked`, `venue_unavailable`, `platform_duplicate` (the platform request is already linked to another event of this venue).

delete.description: Deletes an **archived** event for good, with its quotes, notes, tasks and BEO, after removing it from the connected calendars. Archive it first with `POST /events/{id}/archive`: a live event answers `409 event_not_archived`. An event still referenced by an invoice answers `409 event_has_dependencies`. **Role permission:** `settings.manage`.

post.description: Archives the event like « Archive » in the app (same service): the event becomes read-only and leaves the lists, its open tasks are cancelled, the requests and platform quotes of its request are re-routed, it is removed from the connected calendars and the activity is written. The status is kept. Reversible with `POST /events/{id}/unarchive`; required before `DELETE /events/{id}`. Idempotent (`already_archived: true`). No body. **Role permission:** `data.write`.

already_archived.description: The event was already archived (nothing changed).

post.description: Restores an archived event like « Unarchive » in the app (same service): the tasks the archive cancelled are reopened, the event is published again to the connected calendars and the activity is written. Idempotent (`already_active: true`). No body. **Role permission:** `data.write`.

already_active.description: The event was not archived (nothing changed).

post.description: Same service as the app's status menu: archived events refused, custom stage checked against the workspace's stages, loss and cancellation reasons stored (cleared by any other status), the other `option` events of a group lost when one is confirmed (with `sibling_loss_reason`), `event_confirmed` notification, Slack and calendar sync. Fires the `event.status_changed` / `event.stage_changed` webhooks. **Role permission:** `events.manage`.

stage_id.description: Custom stage under `status` (workspace stages); `null` clears it.

sibling_loss_reason_detail.description: Confirming an event of a group marks its other `option` events `lost` with this reason. Omitted: they stay as they are.

400.description: Validation failed; `details.reason` `invalid_stage` for a stage of another status or workspace.

get.description: Notes of the event, newest first, with their author's name. Not paginated. **Role permission:** none (any member).

post.description: Adds a note by the token owner and a timeline entry. **Role permission:** `data.write`.

get.description: Tasks of the event, newest first. Not paginated. **Role permission:** none (any member).

post.summary: Create a task on an event
post.description: Same as `POST /tasks` with the event of the path. **Role permission:** `data.write`.

get.description: Day-of (on-site) contacts of the event: the people reachable during the event itself, distinct from the booking `contact_person_id`. Primary first, then by `sortOrder`. **Role permission:** none (any member).

put.description: Replaces the whole day-of contact list. The submitted array is the new list: entries with an `id` are updated, entries without one are created, existing rows left out are deleted. **Role permission:** `data.write`.

get.description: Per-day breakdown of a multi-day event with its per-day BEO overrides, by `dayIndex`. A single-day event returns an empty array: its flat fields apply. **Role permission:** none (any member).

put.description: Updates the per-day BEO overrides of existing days, matched on `dayDate`. The days themselves come from the event's dates and `selected_dates` (set on the event): this endpoint never adds or removes a day. A `dayDate` that matches no day is skipped and listed in `skippedDates`. **Role permission:** `data.write`.

skippedDates.description: Submitted days that match no day of the event.

get.description: Which space (room) of the venue the event uses, which day, and at what time. Times are the venue's wall clock (no time zone); a slot without times takes the whole day; an end before the start ends the next day. Ordered by day, then start time (whole-day slots first). **Role permission:** none (any member).

post.description: Books a space of the event's venue for a day, optionally between two times. The space joins the event's `spaces`; a space with slots is only busy during them (conflict checks, availability). The event must have a venue. Pushes the change to the connected calendars. **Role permission:** `data.write`.

400.description: Validation failed: `space_id` is not a space of the event's venue, the event has no venue, only one of the two times is given, or `quote_item_id` is not a line of a quote of this event.

patch.description: Changes the space, day, times, label or quote line of a slot. `null` clears a field; `start_time` and `end_time` both `null` = the whole day. **Role permission:** `data.write`.

Inquiries are dated by their reception.

**Changed in 1.3.0:** this endpoint used to count events by status and by event month over a fixed 12-month window. It now reports inquiries with the page's definitions; the legacy `analytics` map is kept but holds inquiry counts per reception month.
**Role permission:** `reports.view`.

Sales over the period (the Reports page "Sales" tab). Signatures and signed revenue are dated by `confirmed_at`; opportunities, losses and the conversion rate by the event's creation (creation cohort). Conversion rate = confirmed / closed options (confirmed + lost + cancelled). The pipeline is the open options now, whatever the period, valued from their latest quote or expected revenue and weighted by their win probability.

**Changed in 1.3.0:** the legacy top-level fields are kept but use these definitions: `total_events_created` = opportunities created in the period, `total_confirmed` = those confirmed, `conversion_rate` = the conversion rate above (rounded, 0 when no option is closed), `total_revenue_excl_tax` = revenue signed in the period, `total_expected_revenue` = value of the open pipeline. Amounts are in the workspace `currency` (per-currency breakdowns were removed).
**Role permission:** `reports.view`.

Realized revenue over the period (the Reports page "Finance" tab): revenue excl. tax of confirmed events dated by the event's start date (in the event's time zone), cancellation fees included and dated by the cancellation. An event's amount is its confirmed amount, else its latest accepted/signed quote, else the accepted platform amount; `coverage` says how many confirmed events have one. Also returns the current calendar year outlook (realized, booked ahead, forecast with an 80 % range).

**Changed in 1.3.0:** `monthly_accounting` is kept (count and revenue per event month, months with events only) but follows the period and amount rules above.
**Role permission:** `reports.view`.

The first response is the earliest platform reply, quote sent, email sent or information request after reception; failing that, the accept/reject in Joinways (counted as `fallback`). Delivery format, headers, signature and retries are described in the **Webhooks** section above. At most 25 active subscriptions per workspace. **Role permission:** `integrations.manage`.

target_url.description: Public https endpoint that receives the deliveries.

201.description: Subscription created. `secret` is only returned here.

400.description: Validation failed, or `target_url` is not a public https URL.

422.description: Active subscription quota reached (`quota_exceeded`, 25 per workspace).

delete.description: Zapier `performUnsubscribe`. The member who created the hook may always delete it; any other hook of the workspace needs `integrations.manage` (`403` otherwise). An unknown id is a success (idempotent). **Role permission:** `data.write` (own hook) or `integrations.manage`.

404.description: `id` is not a UUID (an unknown UUID is a success).

bearerAuth.description: Paste a token in the `Authorization: Bearer …` header: an **API key** (`jw_…`, created in Settings → Developers → API keys, acting with the role of the member who created it) or an **OAuth 2.1 access token** (`jw_oat_…`). A token is bound to a single workspace.

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.1 authorization code grant with mandatory PKCE (S256). Access tokens are opaque strings prefixed `jw_oat_`, presented as `Authorization: Bearer …`: valid 1 hour with a refresh token (`jw_ort_…`, rotated on each use, 90 days idle), 30 days for a client without the refresh grant. Send `resource=https://joinways.app/api/v1` (RFC 8707). Clients register dynamically or use an https `client_id` (Client ID Metadata Document). Tokens are bound to a single workspace.

scopes.mcp.read: Read the workspace data the member's role can read.
scopes.mcp.write: Create, update, delete and actions within the member's role (implies read).

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional client-generated key (1 to 255 characters, e.g. a UUID v4) that makes the request idempotent for 24 hours: a retry with the same key replays the recorded response (marked `Idempotency-Replayed: true`) instead of executing the operation again. Same key with another body: `422 idempotency_key_reuse`; while the first request runs: `409 idempotency_conflict`. See the **Idempotency** section.

VenueId.name: venueId
VenueId.description: A venue, or a space (room) of a venue.

ReportFrom.name: from
ReportFrom.description: First day included (`YYYY-MM-DD`, workspace time zone). Give together with `to`; without both, the period is the last 6 full months plus the current month (as on the Reports page). A full ISO timestamp is accepted and only its date is kept. Periods longer than 7 years are shortened to the 7 years ending on `to`; the effective period is echoed in `period`.

ReportTo.name: to
ReportTo.description: Last day included (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Give together with `from`.

ReportVenues.name: venues
ReportVenues.description: Comma-separated venue ids (GET /venues) to restrict the report to. Omit for all venues. An id that is not a venue of the workspace is refused with `400`.

ReportCompare.name: compare
ReportCompare.description: Comparison period: `year` (default) = the same days one year earlier; `previous` = the period of the same length just before; `none` = no comparison (every `previous` value is `null`).

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed in the current window (per workspace once authenticated, per IP before).

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

BadRequest.description: Validation failed (`invalid_request`). For a body that fails the schema, `details` holds `formErrors` and `fieldErrors`.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked bearer token (`unauthorized`).

WWW-Authenticate.description: RFC 6750 challenge pointing at the protected resource metadata (RFC 9728).

Forbidden.description: `forbidden`: the token lacks the scope, its owner's role lacks the permission named by the operation, or the workspace has neither the Pro plan nor a trial (`details.reason` `plan_not_eligible`).

ReportsForbidden.description: The token lacks the `mcp.read` scope, or its owner's role lacks the `reports.view` permission (reports carry revenue).

NotFound.description: Not found in this workspace, or the id of the path is not a UUID (`not_found`).

Conflict.description: The state of the record refuses the operation (`conflict`). `details.reason` is a stable code.

EventArchived.description: The event is archived, so read-only (`conflict`, `details.reason` `event_archived`). Unarchive it first (`POST /events/{id}/unarchive`).

error.message: Event is archived: unarchive it before editing it

VenueUnavailable.description: The venue (or a booked space) is in `block` availability mode and the event's days or hours fall on a closure or outside its opening hours. `error.code` is `conflict`; `error.details` carries `reason: venue_unavailable`, `violation` (`VENUE_CLOSED` or `OUTSIDE_HOURS`) and the `closures` / `outside_hours` hit (see GET /venues/{venueId}/conflicts). In `warn` mode the event is saved.

QuoteStateConflict.description: The quote's state refuses the operation (`conflict`); retrying the same call fails the same way until that state changes (except `amendment_in_flight`, transient). `error.details.reason` (see `QuoteErrorReason`): `quote_locked` (signed, invoiced or paid: amend or cancel instead), `quote_signed`, `quote_cancelled`, `quote_not_cancellable`, `quote_has_active_invoice` (credit the invoice first), `quote_has_amendments` (a quote with a live amendment is frozen), `quote_superseded` (a replaced version is history), `amendment_in_flight` (one amendment at a time), `amendment_nested`, `parent_not_active`, `parent_not_signed`, `parent_fully_invoiced`, `quote_changed` (the status changed meanwhile), `invalid_status`, `not_a_platform_version`, `event_closed` (event lost or cancelled), `event_archived`, `platform_quote_read_only` (a platform quote, `source: platform`, is the platform's document: amounts, discounts, currency and lines are read-only, its status only takes `accepted` or `rejected`), `platform_quote_delete_forbidden` (cancel or refuse it instead), `platform_version_signed` (another version is signed), `quote_conflict` (another live contract must be cancelled or refused first).

error.message: This quote is signed or invoiced and can no longer be changed. Create an amendment, or cancel the quote.

PaymentRequired.description: Quotes are not included in the workspace plan (`payment_required`, `details.reason` `quotes_plan_required`).

RateLimited.description: Too many requests (`rate_limited`). `details.reason`: `per-ip`, `per-account-minute`, `per-account-day`, or `email_rate_limited` (email budget). Always carries `Retry-After`: wait that many seconds.

Error.description: Standard error envelope returned on any non-2xx response.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (see the Errors table).

message.description: Human-readable message (do not parse it). Generic on 5xx.

details.description: Structured details: field errors on validation (`formErrors`, `fieldErrors`), the query parameter at fault (`field`), `reason` (a stable code) on refusals, or `null`.

field.description: The parameter or body field at fault.

ErrorReason.description: `details.reason` of an error: snake_case lower case, the same value as the `code` of the matching MCP tool error. One list per domain.

EventErrorReason.description: Events, their sub-resources and the BEO.

LeadErrorReason.description: Leads: convert, merge, link, status, create.

Paginated.description: Envelope wrapping a page of results.

data.description: The page of results (item type depends on the endpoint).

total.description: Total matching items across all pages (`null` only on a page past the last one, when unknown).

WebhookSubscription.description: An outbound webhook subscription (Zapier or custom endpoint).

target_url.description: The endpoint; only its origin (`https://host/…`) without `integrations.manage`.

disabled_at.description: Set after 10 failed deliveries in a row.

EventStatus.description: `option` = pending / tentative, `confirmed` = booked, `lost` = did not convert, `cancelled` = cancelled after booking.

EventSummary.description: An event as listed (`GET /events`, and the `data` of the `event.*` webhooks). Amounts are `null` without `reports.view` or `quotes.manage`.

type.description: Event type, e.g. dinner, wedding, seminar, cocktail.

selected_dates.description: Explicit non-contiguous days of a multi-day event that skips days. When set, `start_date` / `end_date` are the envelope; `null` means a plain contiguous range.

flexible.description: Whether the client's dates are flexible.

confirmed_amount_excl_tax.description: Confirmed amount excl. tax. `null` without revenue access.

assigned_to_account_id.description: The member the event is assigned to (`user_id` of `GET /team-members`).

archived_at.description: Set when the event is archived (read-only).

stage_id.description: Custom stage of the workspace pipeline, under `status`.

event_group_id.description: Groups sibling events (alternative venue options for one client request).

Event.description: The stored event, as returned by `POST /events`, `PATCH /events/{id}` and the conversion of a lead. dietary_notes.description: Diets and allergies (« Contraintes alimentaires »), for the whole event.

beo_public_url.description: Shareable, no-login URL of the public BEO page.

EventDetail.description: `GET /events/{id}`: the event, its company / contact / venue nested (kept for existing integrations) and flat, its booked rooms and its slots.

spaces.description: Spaces of the venue the event books; empty = the whole venue.

slots.description: When the event uses its spaces, day by day. A space without slot is booked every day of the event, all day.

end_date.description: End, after the start. Defaults to `start_date`.

venue_id.description: The venue to book (internally `location_id`); a venue, not a space (pass spaces in `space_ids`). Defaults to the workspace's only active venue; with several, it is required (`400 venue_required`).

company_id.description: An existing company of the workspace.

company_name.description: Company found by name or created. A booking platform name (Aleou, Kactus…) is not a client: it becomes the event `source`.

contact_person_id.description: An existing contact of the workspace, instead of the `contact_*` fields.

contact_email.description: Contact found by email or created.

assigned_to_account_id.description: A member of the workspace (`400 invalid_assignee` otherwise). Defaults to the token owner.

timezone.description: IANA time zone. Defaults to the venue's.

space_ids.description: Spaces (rooms) of the venue the event books; omitted or empty = the whole venue. Ignored for a venue only rented whole (`booked_whole_only`).

selected_dates.description: Non-contiguous days (`YYYY-MM-DD`). With 2 or more distinct days, `start_date` / `end_date` are the time envelope and these days are the event's days.

EventUpdate.description: Every field is optional; omitted fields stay as they are.

stage_id.description: Custom stage under the (new) status; `null` clears it. Needs `events.manage`.

venue_id.description: A venue of the workspace. Changing it without `space_ids` drops the previous venue's spaces; the time zone follows unless given.

space_ids.description: Replaces the booked spaces; `[]` = the whole venue. Ignored for a venue only rented whole (`booked_whole_only`).

quote_to_platform.description: Bill the quotes to the booking platform of `source`. Clears `billing_company_id`.

billing_company_id.description: Bill the quotes to this company instead of the client; `null` = the client. Clears `quote_to_platform`.

selected_dates.description: `[]`, `null` or a single day reverts to a contiguous range.

sent_at.description: When the quote was sent (for a platform quote, when the platform transmitted it).

source.description: `joinways` = written in Joinways. `platform` = a booking platform's own document recorded in Joinways, mostly read from the platform's emails (quote transmitted, with its PDF), or imported once signed. A platform quote is read-only: its amounts, discounts, currency and lines are never edited, it is never deleted nor duplicated, and its status only takes `accepted` or `rejected` through the API; its PDF is the platform's.

source_platform.description: Booking platform the document comes from (platform quote), or the one a Joinways quote was deposited to (e.g. Kactus).

external_reference.description: The platform's own quote number (a platform that renumbers each revision gives each version its own). Unique per event.

superseded_at.description: When the quote was replaced (null while it is live).

discount_percent.description: Global discount in percent. Exclusive with `discount_amount` (send the other as null).

discount_amount.description: Global discount as an amount in the quote currency.

billing_profile_id.description: Billing profile to invoice against; a profile of the workspace (`400` otherwise).

client_email.description: An empty string is stored as `null`.

is_offered.description: Offered (free) line; bypasses the catalog minimum-price check.

event_day.description: 1-based day this line belongs to (multi-day events).

client_selected_at.description: When the client ticked this option on the public quote.

vat.description: Tax rate in %. Omitted, the standard rate of the venue's country (e.g. 0 in the US, 20 in France).

location_item_id.description: Catalog item to price this line from; an item of the workspace (`400` otherwise). The `unit_price` is checked against the catalog minimum price.

Company.description: A client company of the CRM.

state.description: State / province / region (US state, Canadian province…).

enrichment_status.description: Automatic enrichment of the company profile.

enrichment_data.description: What the enrichment found (website, size, sector…).

role.description: Same as `job_title` (send one; both must agree).

PersonUpdate.description: Every field is optional; at least one is required.

location_id.description: The workspace venue the request is for.

inquiry_key.description: Identity of the request (`<platform>:<inquiry id>` or `<platform>:link:<canonical link>`). Same key = same request (siblings across venues).

is_locked.description: Locked by the Free plan monthly allowance (content sealed).

archived_at.description: Deleted (soft) or merged into another lead.

event_id.description: Event the request is on (converted or linked).

requested_space_ids.description: Spaces (rooms) of `location_id` the request asks for.

color.description: Hex color used in the calendar.

event_id.description: An event of the workspace, not archived.

rental_fee.description: Hire fee excl. tax, venue currency (quote reference).

monthly_accounting.description: Legacy — `YYYY-MM` → events and revenue of that event month (months with events only).

year_outlook.description: Current calendar year (workspace time zone), whatever the period.

realized.description: Revenue of events up to today included.

secured.description: Realized + confirmed events to come this year.

from_options.description: Open options dated in the period × probability to sign before the event date (survival model on each option's history). An option without amount counts at its estimated amount (similar confirmed events).

from_unpriced_confirmed.description: Confirmed events still without amount, at their estimated amount × share of past confirmed events that received one.

from_upcoming_inquiries.description: Revenue expected from inquiries not received yet (booking pace of past months).

goal.description: Annual realized-revenue goal of the venues shown, the sum of the 12 monthly goals (same rule as the monthly goal). Amount and progress are null while a month has no goal.

missing_months.description: Months (YYYY-MM) without a goal for the venues shown.

expected_from_upcoming_inquiries.description: Revenue expected from inquiries not received yet (booking pace of past months).

analytics.description: Legacy — `YYYY-MM` → inquiry counts of that reception month.

lost_slot.description: Lost because the date was taken.

processing.description: Time from reception to accept/reject in Joinways (calendar hours).

month_revenue.description: Revenue of confirmed events dated in the current month (event date, as in accounting), which the goal measures.

realized_to_date.description: Events already past, up to today.

forecast.description: Secured revenue plus the month's options weighted by their signing probability, with an 80 % range.

from_options.description: Open options dated in the period × probability to sign before the event date (survival model on each option's history). An option without amount counts at its estimated amount (similar confirmed events).

from_unpriced_confirmed.description: Confirmed events still without amount, at their estimated amount × share of past confirmed events that received one.

from_upcoming_inquiries.description: Revenue expected from inquiries not received yet (booking pace of past months).

like_for_like.description: Month revenue without the venues opened or closed since last year (null when every venue was open both years). A venue is opened since last year when it had no confirmed event in the 12 months up to the same month last year, closed when it had none in the last 12 months.

goal.description: Monthly realized-revenue goal, measured on month_revenue. All venues shown: the workspace goal, else the sum of the venue goals. Venue filter: the sum of the shown venues' goals. A sum is only given when every venue shown has a goal (see goal_missing_venues).

secured_pct.description: Confirmed events of the month / goal.

goal_missing_venues.description: Venues shown without a goal this month while others have one. goal is then null (incomplete goal).

insights.description: Up to 3 computed findings, each with `kind` (`venueDriver`, `sourceVolume`, `venueConversion`, `responseTime`), `tone` (`up`/`down`), `weight` and kind-specific fields (`location_id`, `source_key`, `delta`, `share`, `recent`, `baseline`, `change`, `recent_pct`, `baseline_pct`, `closed`, `recent_minutes`, `baseline_minutes`).

expiring_quotes.description: Options whose quote expires within 7 days.

viewed_quotes.description: Quotes opened at least twice, last viewed within 7 days.

pending_inquiries.description: Inquiries of the last 30 days still to process.

trend.description: 11 past months, the current month and 3 months ahead (revenue by event month).

from_options.description: Open options dated in the period × probability to sign before the event date (survival model on each option's history). An option without amount counts at its estimated amount (similar confirmed events).

from_unpriced_confirmed.description: Confirmed events still without amount, at their estimated amount × share of past confirmed events that received one.

from_upcoming_inquiries.description: Revenue expected from inquiries not received yet (booking pace of past months).

goal.description: Realized-revenue goal of the month for the venues shown (same rule as goal). Null when not set or incomplete.

goal_probability.description: Upcoming months with a goal: probability (0-1) of reaching it, read from the simulated month (same model as goal.probability). Null for past months or without goal.

by_source.description: Top 6 sources by inquiries received over 12 months.

under_1h_rate.description: Answered within one business hour / received.

fallback.description: Answers dated only by the accept/reject fallback.

by_member.description: By the member who gave the first signal.

arrivals.description: Inquiries received by weekday (Monday first) × 2-hour slot, venue local time.

pending.description: Inquiries of the last 30 days still to process (not bound to the period).
